name: 1905 S. Prairie Avenue — the alley building of the house at 1905 (district draft; refined by T-1936)

function.note: The 1911 sheet reads '2-storey brick BARN on the alley'. 1911 labels it a garage or barn; for 1904 the envelope is backcast and its use reconstructed as a stable/coach house. The period description puts Field's "stables and other out-buildings ... in the rear, on the side nearest the lake".

research_note: A DISTRICT DRAFT (T-2330, the owner's district pass of 2026-10-08): a serviceable first model, complete from the street, the walks, the alley and the air, that T-1936 refines in place under this same id. Written by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py from the sheet 28 trace (s28fp-1905-b2), the T-1841 census (s28-1905-rear) and the T-1837 register row frontage-28-055; every height, roof, opening and feature is the draft rules' reconstruction (data/components/prairie_1904/draft_prairie_1904.json; liberty L-draft-prairie-18-20-east-2330).

documented_range.note: The draft claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1841 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Its building and loss dates are the per-building ticket's to read.

position.symbolic_location: 1905 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1905 (data/street_grid/1904.json), east side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 18th to 20th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 28).
position.note: The rear corner of the main body's rectangle (lot frame u 1.000, v -24.750 m from the middle of the rear lot line), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the georeference's independent check is 1.47 m RMS. footprint.note: The main body: the largest rectangle that fits inside the traced main part (u toward the street, v along the front). The building's other rectangles are in draft_plan.

stories.note: The census reading '2-storey brick BARN on the alley': 2 storeys.

construction.note: The trace's fabric colour on the main part: brick.

parts.from: s28fp-1905-b2 p1 (main, brick), rectangle 1 of that part; the part's rectangles cover 81% of its fill

draft_plan.note: Rectangles fitted inside the traced parts by the rules' fit (cell 0.25 m, at most 3 a part, to 90% cover): s28fp-1905-b2 p1 (main, brick), rectangle 1 of that part; the part's rectangles cover 81% of its fill. Roles: the main part's largest rectangle is the main body; a shallow rectangle at the front is a bay; the sheet's ranges, porches and stone fronts keep their roles. Storeys per piece and roof per piece are the draft rules' (reconstructed).

draft_elevation.note: RECONSTRUCTED by the draft rules, family row 'service' overlaid with the frontage row: Second Empire: the register's 'broad brick/stone mansion, mansard and angular corner bay, dormers' and 'central portico'; the conservatory bay and the 1904 fence are T-1904's and T-1905's. Heights are the rules' starting values inside RECONSTRUCTION-RULES.md's ranges; bays, entrance side, chimneys and dormers are counts the family rules choose, and the seed 1178604403 only tints the fabric inside +-6 %.
